title: The adjunct of a morphism, composed with the counit, gives back the morphism
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories, $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ a functor left adjoint to $R:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ with unit $\eta:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}\to RL$ and counit $\varepsilon:LR\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}$ (satisfying the triangle identities $\varepsilon_{LA}\circ L(\eta_A)=\mathrm{id}_{LA}$, $R(\varepsilon_B)\circ\eta_{RB}=\mathrm{id}_{RB}$). For objects $A$ of $\mathcal C$, $B$ of $\mathcal D$ and morphisms $\varphi:LA\to B$, $\psi:A\to RB$, one has $\psi=R(\varphi)\circ\eta_A$ if and only if $\varepsilon_B\circ L(\psi)=\varphi$. In particular the adjunct $\varphi^\sharp=R(\varphi)\circ\eta_A$ of $\varphi$ satisfies $\varepsilon_B\circ L(\varphi^\sharp)=\varphi$.

source.place: Categories, Definition 0037 (definition-adjoint, line 3344) and the paragraph after it: the equivalence of (1) alpha and beta correspond, (2) beta = v(alpha) o unit, (3) alpha = counit o u(beta); Lemma 0038 (lemma-unit-counit-relations, line 3523) for the triangle identities
